panels.title: Overview — is EDDI healthy right now?
Agents
panels.description: `eddi_agents_deployed` — agents currently in a deployed state.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: `eddi_processing_conversation_count` — turns being processed right now.

panels.title: Turns/sec
panels.description: Rate of `eddi_conversation_processing_count_total` — pipeline throughput.

panels.title: Tool success
panels.description: success / (success + failure). Cached and rate-limited calls are excluded — they are neither a success nor a failure of the tool itself.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(eddi_tool_execution_success_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(increase(eddi_tool_execution_success_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)) + (sum(increase(eddi_tool_execution_failure_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)), 1e-9) and on() ((sum(increase(eddi_tool_execution_success_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)) + (sum(increase(eddi_tool_execution_failure_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0))) > 0

panels.title: Cache hits
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_hits_total` / (hits + misses).

targets.expr: (sum(increase(eddi_tool_cache_hits_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(increase(eddi_tool_cache_hits_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)) + (sum(increase(eddi_tool_cache_misses_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)), 1e-9) and on() ((sum(increase(eddi_tool_cache_hits_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)) + (sum(increase(eddi_tool_cache_misses_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0))) > 0

panels.title: Task errors/sec
panels.description: Rate of `eddi_pipeline_task_errors_total` across every lifecycle task.

panels.title: Tool spend
panels.description: `eddi_tool_costs_accrued` gauge — dollars accrued since process start.

panels.title: Gate verified
panels.description: 1 when every provisioned Platform Operator version last read back with a sound approval gate. 0 also before any report has arrived (fresh deployment, operator never activated). min, so one unverified replica reads 0. Alert EddiOperatorGateRegressed fires on a 1 -> 0 transition.

panels.title: LLM — Per-call latency, tokens and errors
LLM call latency (p95) by provider and model
panels.description: `eddi_llm_request_duration_seconds` — every provider call, not just cascade steps. Counts attempts: a retried turn contributes more than one sample.

panels.title: LLM token rate by type
panels.description: `eddi_llm_tokens_total` — input vs output tokens per second. Do not add to `eddi_llm_cascade_tokens_total`; a cascading task reports through both.

targets.expr: sum by (provider, model, type) (rate(eddi_llm_tokens_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: LLM error rate by exception
panels.description: `eddi_llm_request_errors_total` — failed attempts, tagged with the exception's simple name. `ChatTimeoutException` is the configured wall-clock `timeout` firing.

targets.expr: sum by (provider, error) (rate(eddi_llm_request_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: LLM call outcome mix
panels.description: `eddi_llm_request_duration_seconds_count` split by outcome — the success/error ratio of actual provider calls.

panels.title: Conversation lifecycle rate
panels.description: Every `eddi_conversation_*_count_total` counter.

panels.title: Lifecycle latency (avg)
panels.description: `_seconds_sum / _seconds_count` for each lifecycle timer. These timers publish no histogram buckets, so a true percentile is not available — this is the interval mean.

panels.title: Lifecycle latency (peak)
panels.description: `_seconds_max` — the slowest single observation in each decay window.

panels.title: Conversations in flight
panels.description: `eddi_processing_conversation_count`, and `eddi_conversation_abandoned_running` — turns the agent-timeout watchdog gave up on whose pipeline is still running (normally 0).

panels.title: Agents deployed
panels.description: `eddi_agents_deployed`

panels.title: Conversation listing: owner-scan exhausted, orphans skipped
panels.description: `eddi_conversations_listing_owner_scan_exhausted_total` — a conversation listing gave up before filling the requested page. Sustained non-zero means the owner filter is scanning too much; the caller sees a short page. `eddi_conversations_listing_orphaned_descriptors_total` — descriptors a listing left out because their conversation memory no longer exists. Common on a database carried over from 5.x; the listing is correct either way, but a steady rate means those descriptors are scanned on every listing.

panels.title: Session checkpoints by action
panels.description: `eddi_session_checkpoint_count_total` by `action` — session fork/snapshot activity.

panels.title: Coordinator queue depth
panels.description: `eddi_coordinator_queue_depth` — conversations waiting for a slot. Sustained growth means arrival outpaces processing.

panels.title: Coordinator active conversations
panels.description: `eddi_coordinator_active_conversations`

panels.title: Coordinator throughput
panels.description: Rate of `eddi_coordinator_total_processed_total`; of turns refused before they were queued (`eddi_turn_rejected_total`: `in_flight_limit` answered 503 `capacity_exceeded`, `caller_timed_out` answered 408 because the request waited out `systemRuntime.agentTimeoutInSeconds` for a thread); and of queued turns dropped unrun because their caller had already timed out (`eddi_turn_skipped_total`).

panels.title: Task duration P50 / P95 / P99
panels.description: `eddi_pipeline_task_duration_seconds_bucket`. This is the only EDDI timer that calls `publishPercentileHistogram()`, so it is the only one where a real quantile exists.

panels.title: Task duration P99 by task type
panels.description: Which lifecycle task is slow. Note the label is `task_type` — Micrometer converts the `task.type` tag key to an underscore.

panels.title: Task error rate by error type
panels.description: `eddi_pipeline_task_errors_total` by `error_type`.

panels.title: Task errors by task and error type (5m)
panels.description: Exact failing task ids. `increase` over 5m, top 25.

panels.title: Dead-lettered turns (in-memory coordinator)
panels.description: Turns that failed after they had started. The rate is cumulative across purges; 'retained' is what GET /administration/coordinator/dead-letters lists now (capped by eddi.coordinator.max-dead-letters). In cluster mode 'retained' is the shared dead-letter stream's count.

panels.title: Turn executor load
panels.description: Conversation work on the worker pool (managed) and the nested virtual-thread executor. Sustained 'waiting for a thread' means the pool is saturated (alert EddiExecutorSaturated).

panels.title: Quarkus worker pool
panels.description: Quarkus' own view of its worker pools: blocking REST requests and work dispatched through Vert.x. Turns submitted by the coordinator are on 'Turn executor load'.

panels.title: Execution outcomes
panels.description: The outcomes of `ToolExecutionService.executeToolWrapped()`. `success` and `failure` partition every wrapped call between them; `cached` refines `success`, and `ratelimited` and `timeout` refine `failure`, so those three series are counted twice in the stack rather than being alternatives. `repeat refused` counts calls the tool repeat guard refused before execution; they never reach `executeToolWrapped()` and are additive to the partition.

panels.title: Tool calls by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_calls_total` by `tool`.

panels.title: Execution latency by tool (avg)
panels.description: `eddi_tool_execution_duration_seconds` mean per tool.

panels.title: Execution latency (peak)
panels.description: `_seconds_max` per tool.

panels.title: Failures by tool (1h)
panels.description: Which tools actually break.

panels.title: Budget exceeded
panels.description: `eddi_tool_budget_exceeded_total` — a conversation hit its cost ceiling and the call was refused.

panels.title: Cumulative tool spend
panels.description: `eddi_tool_costs_accrued` gauge — dollars accrued since process start.

panels.title: Spend rate by tool
panels.description: Rate of `eddi_tool_costs_total{tool}` — dollars per second, per tool.

panels.title: Spend by tool (24h)
panels.description: Where the money went.

panels.title: Abandoned tool workers
panels.description: Tool executions that outlived their `toolTimeoutsMs` bound, were interrupted, did not stop, and are still running with nobody waiting on them. A spike is one hung call; a line that climbs and never returns to zero is a tool leaking workers, each still holding the conversation memory of a turn that has already been answered. Zero is the normal reading — `cancel(true)` unwinds any tool blocked in interruptible I/O immediately, so a non-zero value means a native call or a tight loop. Pair it with `eddi_tool_execution_timeout_total` to see which tool.

panels.title: Hits vs misses
panels.description: Aggregate `eddi_tool_cache_hits_total` / `_misses_total`.

panels.title: Cache size
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_size` — live entry count.

panels.title: Hits by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_hits_by_tool_total`

panels.title: Misses by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_misses_by_tool_total`

panels.title: Puts by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_puts_by_tool_total`

panels.title: Cache bypassed by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_bypassed_total` — caching was enabled but no identity could scope the entry, so both read and write were skipped. Sustained non-zero means calls arrive with neither a user id nor a conversation id and pay full tool cost every time. Investigate the caller rather than widening cache scope.

panels.title: Cache get / put latency (avg)
panels.description: `eddi_tool_cache_{get,put}_duration_seconds` mean.

panels.title: Denied by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_ratelimit_denied_total` by `tool`.

panels.title: Remaining capacity by tool
panels.description: `eddi_tool_ratelimit_remaining` — tokens left in the most constrained bucket for each tool. Approaching zero means the next call is about to be denied.

panels.title: Cascade token rate by provider
panels.description: `eddi_llm_cascade_tokens_total` — tokens/sec.

panels.title: Cascade spend rate by provider
panels.description: `eddi_llm_cascade_cost_total`

panels.title: Cascade confidence (avg)
panels.description: `eddi_llm_cascade_confidence` distribution summary. Falling confidence means the cascade is escalating more often.

panels.title: Streaming downgraded by reason
panels.description: `eddi_llm_streaming_downgraded_total` — a streaming request fell back to non-streaming (e.g. `reason=tools_enabled`).

panels.title: Structured output outcomes (convertToObject)
panels.description: `eddi_llm_output_total` — how each `convertToObject` reply parsed: `valid`, `repaired` (fence/prose stripped), `invalid` (stored as a raw string), `empty` or `schema_mismatch` (parsed, but wrong shape). A rising `invalid` or `schema_mismatch` rate points at a prompt, schema or model-version problem.

panels.title: Streaming without partials / timed out
panels.description: `eddi_llm_streaming_no_partials_total` — the stream produced no incremental tokens, so the user waited for a single block. `eddi_llm_stream_timeouts_total` — EDDI abandoned a stream at its own backstop, by path (legacy | tool_loop); counted when EDDI gives up, not when the provider eventually reports it.

panels.title: Tool-context evictions by outcome
panels.description: `eddi_llm_tool_context_evictions_total` — tool-result exchanges dropped to fit the token budget, incremented by the number evicted. `outcome=still_over_budget` means eviction ran and the context is *still* too large, so the model is about to see a truncated history. Registered through `Metrics.globalRegistry`.

panels.title: Cascade executions by agent mode
panels.description: Cascade runs started, split by whether agent mode (tool calling) was in use. The denominator for every other panel in this row.

panels.title: Escalations by reason
panels.description: Why the cascade moved to a more expensive model: low_confidence, timeout, or an error type. A cascade that never escalates is paying for steps it does not use; one that always escalates is paying twice for every turn.

panels.title: Accepted step (which model actually answered)
panels.description: Index of the cascade step whose answer was accepted. Mass at step 0 means the cheap model is carrying the load — the whole point of cascading. Mass at the last step means the cascade is pure overhead.

panels.title: Step errors by provider and type
panels.description: Errors raised by an individual cascade step, tagged with the provider that failed. These are absorbed by escalation, so they do not surface as request failures — this panel is the only place they are visible.

targets.expr: sum by (provider, type) (rate(eddi_llm_cascade_step_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: LLM failures by class and model
panels.description: Failed LLM calls (cascade steps) by failure class: TRANSIENT, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, AUTH, BAD_REQUEST, CONTEXT_TOO_LONG, MODEL_NOT_FOUND, TIMEOUT, UNKNOWN. QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, AUTH and MODEL_NOT_FOUND are systemic: they will fail every turn until someone acts.

panels.title: Turn deadline exceeded by stage
panels.description: `eddi_llm_turn_deadline_exceeded_total` - a layer stopped because the turn's deadline (agent turnDeadlineMs or the X-EDDI-Turn-Deadline-Ms header) left no room: attempt = a retry not started, sleep = a backoff that would not fit, attempt_timeout = an attempt abandoned at the budget, cascade = no further cascade step, httpcall / httpcall_retry = an HTTP call refused or a retry skipped. Non-zero means turns are being cut short to answer in time.

panels.title: Cancelled LLM attempts and steps
panels.description: `eddi_llm_cancelled_total` - an attempt or cascade step was abandoned on timeout and its future cancelled (scope = attempt | cascade_step). The provider request is also bounded by the clamped model timeout; a steady rate here means timeouts are being hit, not just configured.

panels.title: Ceiling exceeded (cost / duration)
panels.description: Cascade runs cut short because the configured cost or duration ceiling was hit. Non-zero means users are receiving the best answer obtained so far rather than the best answer available.

panels.title: LLM fallbacks served (onError / responseValidation)
panels.description: `eddi_llm_recovery_total` — turns answered with the configured fallback instead of a model answer. `trigger=onError` is a failed model phase absorbed by `onError: fallback`; `trigger=validation` is a `responseValidation` action of `fallback`. A rising rate means users are seeing the apology: read `llm:error:<taskId>` on the step for the cause.

panels.title: LLM same-model re-asks and escalations (responseValidation retry)
panels.description: `eddi_llm_recovery_total` with `action=retry` or `action=escalate` — what the `retry` actions of `responseValidation` did. `retry` outcomes: `recovered` (the re-ask fixed the reply), `still_invalid`, `failed` (the re-ask itself errored), or why a re-ask was skipped (`skipped_budget`, `skipped_no_time`, `skipped_cost`, `skipped_breaker`). `escalate` / `invalid_output` is a cascade step that handed over to the next model after its re-asks. Many `still_invalid` or `escalate` per `trigger` means a prompt, schema or model problem, not noise: every re-ask is a billed call.

panels.title: LLM circuit breaker transitions and skipped turns
panels.description: `eddi_llm_circuit_total` counts state changes of a model's circuit breaker (`state=open|half_open|closed`, `class` = what opened it: `INVALID_OUTPUT`, `BAD_REQUEST`, `MODEL_NOT_FOUND`, `AUTH`, `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`); every `open` is also one ERROR log line naming agent, version, provider, model and reason. `eddi_llm_circuit_skipped_total` counts turns that did not call the model because its circuit was open: a cascade went on to the next step, a task without one took its `onError` path. Any `open` rate is a model that needs attention (a revoked key, a retired model, a prompt it cannot answer); `skipped` says how many turns that cost.

panels.title: LLM circuits open right now
panels.description: `eddi_llm_circuit_open` — the number of model circuits on each node that are open or half-open at this moment (in-memory, per node; a restart or an hour without traffic resets a circuit to closed). Non-zero means at least one model is being skipped: see the ERROR log of the transition for which one and why.

panels.title: Tool-result guardrail by action
panels.description: `eddi_guardrail_toolresult_count_total` by `action` — what the guardrail did to the result.

panels.title: Tool-result guardrail by source
panels.description: …and which tool source triggered it.

panels.title: MCP response truncation
panels.description: `eddi_mcp_response_truncation_count_total` by `strategy` — oversized tool responses being cut down before they reach the model.

panels.title: Counterweight activations by level
panels.description: `eddi_counterweight_activation_count_total` by `level` (normal / cautious / strict).

panels.title: Strict counterweight downgraded
panels.description: `eddi_counterweight_strict_downgraded_total` — a strict counterweight could not be honoured and was reduced. Worth alerting on if the strict level is a compliance control.

panels.title: Identity masking applied
panels.description: `eddi_identity_masking_applied_total` — outbound payloads with identity masked.

panels.title: Turn-level pause / resume by surface
panels.description: `eddi_hitl_pause_count_total` / `_resume_count_total` by `surface` (`regular` = single conversation, `group` = group discussion). A pause rate that outruns resume means approvals are piling up.

panels.title: Approval timeouts by surface
panels.description: `eddi_hitl_timeout_count_total` — nobody answered in time and the timeout policy fired.

panels.title: Tool-call gate pause / resume
panels.description: `eddi_hitl_tool_pause_count_total` and `eddi_hitl_tool_resume_count_total{verdict}` — the per-tool-call approval gate.

panels.title: Approval rule matches
panels.description: `eddi_hitl_rule_matched_total` by `match` — which `hitlConfig.toolApprovals` `requireApproval` pattern matched, counted once per distinct rule per gated call. A pattern that never appears here is dead config.

panels.title: Operator write approvals by decision
panels.description: `eddi_operator_write_approval_total` by `decision` (approved / rejected / timeout) — one per gated operator write the moment it resolves.

panels.title: Tool gate guards by guard
panels.description: `eddi_hitl_tool_guard_count_total` by `guard` — a safety guard (e.g. `pause_cap`) stopped the gate rather than the human.

panels.title: MCP approval decisions
panels.description: `eddi_mcp_hitl_decision_total` by `verdict`.

panels.title: MCP approvals cancelled
panels.description: `eddi_mcp_hitl_cancelled_total`

panels.title: MCP pending-approval listings
panels.description: `eddi_mcp_hitl_pending_listed_total`

panels.title: Pending approvals
panels.description: Conversations paused for a human (approval or input), read from the conversation store every eddi.hitl.metrics.refresh-interval. Every replica reports the store-wide number, hence max. Saturates at 1000.

panels.title: Oldest pending approval
panels.description: How long the oldest pending approval has waited. Alert EddiApprovalWaitingLong fires past 24 h.

panels.title: Rejections under onRejection: REVISE
panels.description: `eddi_hitl_revision_total{outcome}` — what a rejected rule pause did under `hitlConfig.onRejection: REVISE`: `revised`, or why it skipped (`no_note`, `automated`, `no_answer`, `exhausted`, `failed`). A rising `failed` share means revisions are refused by the spend gate, the model or a guardrail.

panels.title: Discussion failure rate
panels.description: failures / started.

panels.title: Discussion duration
panels.description: `eddi_group_discussion_duration_seconds`.

panels.title: Discussion outcomes
panels.description: How discussions end.

panels.title: Facilitator moves by outcome
panels.description: `eddi_group_facilitator_moves_total` by `outcome` — `proposed` is every move the model asked for, `executed` the ones allowed, `rejected` the ones the bounded-move config refused. A large proposed/executed gap means the facilitator is repeatedly attempting moves it is not permitted to make.

panels.title: Facilitator moves by move type (1h)
panels.description: `move` is bounded to the FacilitatorMove enum names plus UNKNOWN, so this label is safe to group by.

panels.title: Group cost
panels.description: `eddi_group_cost_dollars` gauge.

panels.title: Cost ceiling hits
panels.description: `eddi_group_cost_ceiling_hit_total` — a discussion was cut off by its budget. Already `_total`-suffixed in source, so Micrometer does not add another.

panels.title: Member pauses skipped
panels.description: `eddi_group_member_pause_skipped_count_total` — a HUMAN member's turn did not pause when it should have.

panels.title: Team cadence runs
panels.description: `eddi_team_cadence_runs_{started,skipped}_total` — scheduled standing-team cadences.

panels.title: Team cadence writebacks & reclaims
panels.description: Reclaimed claims mean a cadence holder died mid-run and another node took over.

panels.title: Tasks returned for rework
panels.description: `eddi_group_task_reworks_total` — tasks VERIFY sent back to their member with the verifier's feedback (`maxReworks`).

panels.title: Unparseable VERIFY verdicts
panels.description: `eddi_group_verify_unparseable_total` — verifier replies that could not be parsed; every task of that pass was auto-verified (fail-open). Should stay near zero: a steady rate means the moderator's model ignores the verdict format.

title: E.D.D.I — Full Metrics Reference (1/2)
description: Every meter E.D.D.I registers with Micrometer, grouped by subsystem. Counters are shown as rates, timers as mean and peak from _seconds_sum/_seconds_count/_seconds_max. Only eddi_pipeline_task_duration publishes histogram buckets, so it is the only EDDI timer with true percentiles. Companion to the Operations Command Center dashboard.
